summary: 1931 steel fire tower in Stratham Hill Park, burned in 1997 and rebuilt in 1998; voters approved $250,000 for repairs in 2026. The 45-ft observation deck is open to visitors.

facts.design: 53-ft steel tower with a 10 by 10 ft cab and a public observation platform at 45 ft (register)

staffing.status: not staffed; state staffing ended in 1976 and the town maintains the tower

access.note: In Stratham Hill Park; hikers climb to the 45-ft observation deck (2026 newspaper article).

visit.trail_note: Public observation platform at 45 ft; the view includes the Squamscott River and Great Bay

events.note: Edward Tuck gave about 70 acres to the town as a park, in memory of Amos Tuck
Built by the N.H. Department of Forests and Lands on the park land
Fire warden Herman Wilbur reopened the tower
State staffing ended; the town took over the park and tower
Arson fire; the register says the wooden cab burned and a metal cab replaced it. The 2026 article says the tower burned in arson in 1997
Town replaced the burned structure with a $20,000 steel structure
September 2023 HEB Engineers report recommended concrete, bolt and coating repairs
Voters approved $250,000 in March for repair and repainting; work scheduled to begin in fall 2026

corrections.why: The register gives a 53-ft steel tower, which is 16.2 m. No source found supports 24.0 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes a steel tower with a wooden cab. The 2026 article says the original structure was built of wood. The story reports both.

The register says the wooden cab burned in 1997. The 2026 article says the tower was rebuilt twice after arson, burned in the 1980s and again in 1997, and was replaced in 1998 with a steel structure. The 1980s fire has no year in the sources, so no event date is given for it. The town page says the tower burned down twice.

A December 1973 item says state use was phased out after a watchman retired after 16 years. The register and the 2026 article say state staffing ended in 1976. A 1977 memorial notice gives 15 years of service.
The register gives 273 ft (83 m) for the summit. The town page says the hill is about 288 feet tall. The register's figure is kept; the two measures may differ.

sources.title: Stratham's historic fire tower set for repairs after voters approve $250K

notes_for_editor: Height: the record's 24.0 m matches no source; the register's 53-ft steel tower (16.2 m) is proposed, though it is not stated whether 53 ft includes the cab. Elevation: register 273 ft summit vs town page 'about 288 feet tall' for the hill; the register figure is kept. Material: register says steel tower with wooden cab; 2026 article says the original was built of wood. Fires: 1997 is in two sources; the 1980s fire is in the 2026 article only, with no year. Staffing end: 1976 (register, 2026 article) vs a 1973 item and a 1977 memorial (15 vs 16 years). Agency: the register lists the Stratham Fire Department; the 2026 article says the Select Board acted on a Public Works recommendation and the town maintains the park and tower; agency left as the register has it. A 2001 Seacoastonline item on an arson charge for the 1997 fire appeared in search results but returned HTTP 403, so it is not used. Not verified: current climbing rules, hours, or whether the observation deck is open in winter. No photos added.
